title: GMAT Verbal: Reading Comprehension & Critical Reasoning
summary: GMAT Focus Verbal dropped Sentence Correction — it's now 23 questions of Reading Comprehension and Critical Reasoning, all about logic.

nodes.label: No Sentence Correction
nodes.note: Grammar item type removed in Focus

chunks.heading: Grammar's gone — it's reasoning now
chunks.body: GMAT Focus Verbal has **just two question types: Reading Comprehension and Critical Reasoning**. **Sentence Correction was removed**, so pure grammar drills no longer help — the section is entirely about **understanding and evaluating arguments**.
chunks.realExample: If your old prep leaned on memorising idiom and modifier rules for Sentence Correction, redirect that time to Critical Reasoning logic — those points don't exist anymore.
chunks.memoryHook: No more Sentence Correction. GMAT Verbal = reading + reasoning only.

chunks.heading: Critical Reasoning — find the argument's skeleton
chunks.body: You read a **short argument** and answer a question: strengthen it, weaken it, find the assumption, or spot the flaw. The key skill is separating the **conclusion** from the **evidence**, then seeing the **assumption** that links them.
chunks.realExample: 'Sales rose after we changed the logo, so the logo caused the rise.' The unstated assumption is 'nothing else changed'. Weaken it by naming another cause (a price cut, a holiday).
chunks.memoryHook: Split conclusion from evidence, then attack the assumption between them.

chunks.heading: Reading Comprehension — map, don't memorise
chunks.body: Passages are dense but short. **Read for structure** — main point, how each paragraph functions, the author's tone — rather than memorising details. Then return to the text to answer specific questions; **every answer must be supported by the passage**.
chunks.realExample: Jot a two-word label per paragraph ('problem', 'counter-view', 'author's fix'). When a question asks about paragraph 3, your map sends you straight there instead of rereading everything.
chunks.memoryHook: Map the passage's structure. Answers hide in specific lines, not your memory.

chunks.heading: Pace: about two minutes each
chunks.body: 23 questions in 45 minutes is roughly **under two minutes each**, and Reading Comprehension passages serve **several questions**, so time spent understanding a passage pays back across its question set. It's **adaptive** — steady accuracy beats rushing.
chunks.realExample: Invest 3 minutes truly understanding a passage that has 4 questions, and each question then takes 45 seconds — far better than skimming and re-reading for every question.
chunks.memoryHook: Understand the passage once; it pays back across all its questions.

recall.q: What two question types make up GMAT Focus Verbal?
recall.a: Reading Comprehension and Critical Reasoning — Sentence Correction was removed.

recall.q: What is the core skill in Critical Reasoning?
recall.a: Separating the conclusion from the evidence and identifying the assumption that links them.

recall.q: How should you read GMAT Reading Comprehension passages?
recall.a: For structure — main point, each paragraph's function and tone — then return to the text for specifics.

recall.q: How do you weaken an argument in Critical Reasoning?
recall.a: Attack its assumption — for example, by naming an alternative cause the argument overlooked.

recall.q: Why is understanding a passage upfront efficient?
recall.a: Each Reading Comprehension passage serves several questions, so upfront understanding pays back across the set.
